newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 19.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Sept 19.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning.
** The International Monetary Fund (IMF) plays down concerns that modest U.S. interest rate increase would spark massive, bone-jarring sell-off in U.S. stocks and bond prices or in emerging markets
** India's hopes of resolving bad loan problems at its banks over the next two or three years are probably too optimistic, the IMF says in a report
** The Reserve Bank of India sets guidelines for divestment of thinly traded stocks by foreign funds and expatriate Indians

** Coffee production in 14 Asian countries will rise to 21.18 million bags in the 2000/2001 season from 17.56 million in 1995/96, but output in India and the Philippines should be flat to lower, analyst tells World Coffee Conference in Hamburg
** Indian industrial production in six leading infrastructure sectors increased by 2.2 percent in August over the same month in 1995, a government statement said on Wednesday
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opened little changed at 35.72/73 per dollar and seen range-bound, dealers say
** On Wednesday, Indian shares finished higher on fund purchases in index-linked stocks and aided by a technical correction, traders said
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index .BSESN closed 66.64 points, or 1.99 percent, higher at 3,414.01 after sliding to 3,323.80
** The 100-share National index added 11.07 points, or 0.73 percent, at 1,523.49
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index firmed 23.0 points, or 2.37 percent, to 994
** The Delhi share index rose 21.81 points to 764.76
** The Calcutta index .CALSN rose 9.19 points to 439.42
** The Madras index .MDSI added 9.57 points to 3,449.15
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index JCEAI rose 1.70 points, or 2.45 percent, to 69.85 with the premium over the local market at 13.86 percent
